answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to hold a distinct sealed physical deposit in a bonded warehouse. A licensed custodian seals a specimen—a tundra soil core, a rock containing crystal, or an opal fragment—with a tamper-evident serial, and a public ledger accepts one active identity per serial. Extra identities need extra deposits, each paying storage and inspection cost C per period. With per-period reward capped at R, n sybils earn n(R-C), so cloning is profitable only while R>C; custodian collusion or duplicate seals remain the weakness.
